newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish union leaders lay wreath for May Day dead.
newsitem.headline: Turkish union leaders lay wreath for May Day dead.

text.p: Turkish trade union leaders laid a wreath on Thursday in Istanbul's main square in memory of 37 people killed at a May Day rally there 20 years ago.

Police cordoned off Taksim Square with armoured cars and so-called "robocops" -- police with plastic body armour -- for about 150 trade unionists carrying a wreath of red carnations which they laid at a monument.
No one was ever charged for the deaths on May Day, 1977, when a gunman fired on protesters from a building above the square. Most of the victims were crushed to death in the resulting stampede.

"Twenty years ago today, 37 workers died in this place. It has now become clear that their killers were the gangs within the state which came out into the open with the events of Susurluk," said Kemal Daysal, general secretary of the DISK labour confederation.
A security scandal which erupted after a car crash near the town of Susurluk last year has led to allegations that the state used right-wing gangs to murder political enemies.

Security officials planned tight security in Istanbul this year after the death of three people in May Day rioting last year. Damage amounted to $2 million. Twelve thousand policemen backed by more than 2,000 soldiers were on duty.
